αἰγιόχοιο: αἰγίοχος — aegis-bearing (of Zeus); epic gen. sg. -οιο (= Attic -ου); meaning disputed: usually ’holding the αἰγίς (goatskin shield)’, other derivations were proposed in antiquity
αἰετὸς: ἀετός — eagle; masc. nom. sg., epic αἰετός (= Attic ἀετός)
αἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj., epic/dialectal by-form αἰ (used before κε)
αἶαν: Αἴας — Ajax, son of Telamon; masc. voc. sg. Αἶαν
αὐδήν: αὐδή — voice, human speech; fem. acc. sg., accusative of respect: ’in voice’ · also as the direct object of a verb of hearing (θεοῦ ἔκλυεν αὐδήν ’heard the voice of the god’)
αὐτή: αὐτός — self; fem. nom. sg., intensive, stressing the subject herself: ’(you) yourself’ · also intensive, 1st person: ’I myself’ (αὐτή μιν πόμπευον ’I myself escorted him’)
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’ · also intensive with a noun, masc. gen. sg.: ’Alcinous himself’ (αὐτοῦ Ἀλκινόοιο) · also reflexive intensive gen. sg. after a personal pronoun: σέο τ’ αὐτοῦ ’and of yourself’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun of a thing, ’from it’, after ἐκ (ἐκ δ’ αὐτοῦ πείρατ’ ἀνήφθω, of the mast) · also masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive sense, ’his own’: αὐτοῦ ἐνεύναιον ’his own bedding’, αὐτοῦ βώτορες ’his own herdsmen’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun with a noun, ’his’: ὀστέα δ’ αὐτοῦ ’and his bones’ · also intensive gen. sg. with a demonstrative and noun: τοῦδ’ αὐτοῦ λυκάβαντος ’this very year’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun of a thing, ’upon it’, after ἐπί (ἐπ’ αὐτοῦ, of a stool) · also gen. sg. pronoun of comparison after a comparative: ’than he’ (προγενέστερος αὐτοῦ ’older than he’) · also masc. gen. sg. after περί: ’about himself’ (περί τ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ πάντων) · also plain gen. sg. pronoun governed by ἄγχι ’near’: ’him’ (ἄγχι δ’ αὐτοῦ ’close beside him’) · also gen. sg. in a genitive absolute with a participle: ’with him himself still living’ (αὐτοῦ ζώοντος) · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, ’him’, governed by ἰθύς: ’straight towards him’ (ἰθὺς κίεν αὐτοῦ)
αὐτόθι: αὐτόθι — here, on the spot, right there; adv.
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg.: ’himself’ · also masc. nom. sg. with a 1st-person subject: ’myself’ (ἐγὼν αὐτός) · also masc. nom. sg. with a 2nd-person subject: ’yourself’ (εἰδήσεις δὲ καὶ αὐτός ’you will see for yourself’) · also masc. nom. sg., of a thing: ’it itself’ (αὐτὸς … σίδηρος ’iron of itself’)

αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
βάλεν: βάλλω — throw, cast; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, in tmesis with ἀμφί: ’threw about’ · also in tmesis with ἐπί (βάλεν δ’ ἐπὶ ... ἑκάστῳ = ἐπέβαλε): ’threw over, cast upon’ · also in tmesis with παρά (πάρ … βάλεν = παρέβαλε): ’threw beside, set before’ · also without tmesis, with κε, unreal past: ’would have hurled’ (κε … βάλεν … ποτὶ πέτρας ’would have dashed her against the rocks’) · also in tmesis with ἐν (ἐν … βάλεν = ἐνέβαλε): ’cast into, sent upon’ (φύζαν … βάλεν ’sent panic upon’) · also plain aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, with no tmesis: ’let fall’ (δάκρυ χαμαὶ βάλεν ’let a tear fall to the ground’) · also plain aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, ’hit, struck’, the target or the weapon given: σκοπὸν … βάλεν ’hit a mark’, βάλεν ἰῷ ’struck with an arrow’
βιότοιο: βίοτος — life, livelihood; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γένοιτο: γίγνομαι — become, happen, turn out; aor. opt. 3 sg. (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’) · also aor. opt. 3 sg. in a wish with μή: μὴ ... φίλον γένοιτο ’may it not prove pleasing’ · also aor. opt. 3 sg. in a wish after αἲ γάρ: αἲ γὰρ τοῦτο γένοιτο ’would that this might happen’ · also aor. opt. 3 sg. in a wish after εἰ γάρ: εἰ γὰρ … ἔρις γένοιτο ’if only a contest might arise’ · also aor. opt. 3 sg. in a fear clause after μή: ’lest it come to be’ (μὴ … ἀμφαδὰ ἔργα γένοιτο ’lest the matter become public’) · also aor. opt. 3 sg., potential with κε: ’it would be’ · also aor. opt. 3 sg., potential with ἄν: ’would become’ (ἡμῖν δ’ ἂν ἐλέγχεα ταῦτα γένοιτο ’and to us these would become reproaches’) · also aor. opt. 3 sg. in a wish after a hortatory subj., no particle: ’let it arise, may it come about’ (βοὴ δ’ ὤκιστα γένοιτο ’and let a cry go up quickly’)
γένοντο: γίγνομαι — become, come to pass; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἐγένοντο)
γένος: γένος — stock, race, lineage, offspring; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg., governed by μετά: ’after (blood and) lineage’ · also neut. acc. sg., object of εὔχομαι: ’descent, birth’ (γένος εὔχομαι ’I declare my birth’) · also neut. acc. sg. of respect: ’by birth’ (ἐξ Ἰθάκης γένος εἰμί ’I am of Ithaca by birth’)
γέρων: γέρων — old man; masc. nom. sg.
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γλαυκώπιδι: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena, ’gleaming-eyed’ (sense uncertain); fem. dat. sg.
γλαυκώπιδος: γλαυκῶπις — gleaming-eyed (standing epithet of Athena); fem. gen. sg.
γλαυκῶπις: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena: ’gleaming-eyed’ (or ’owl-eyed’; sense uncertain); fem. nom. sg.
δάκρυ: δάκρυ — tear; neut. acc. sg., used collectively: ’tears’ · also elided δάκρυ’ = δάκρυα, neut. acc. pl. · also literal sg. with an attributive adjective, not collective: θαλερὸν δάκρυ ’a swelling tear’ · also literal sg., no adjective: ’a tear’ (ἀπομόρξατο δάκρυ ’wiped away a tear’)
δέμας: δέμας — bodily form, frame; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect: ’in body’ · also neut. acc. sg., direct object or in apposition: ’body’ (εἶδός τε δέμας τε ’form and body’)
δέος: δέος — fear; also, of the thing feared, danger; neut. nom./acc. sg.
δεισάντων: δείδω — fear, dread; aor. part. act. masc./neut. gen. pl. (same form in Attic): ’of those who feared’
διαπρὸ: διαπρό — right through, clean through; adv. (διά + πρό)
διείρεαι: διέρομαι — ask closely about, inquire about (intensive of ἔρομαι); pres. mid. 2 sg.
διὰ: διά — through, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: διὰ … τινάξῃ = διατινάξῃ ’shake apart, shatter’ · also + acc., causal, ’through, thanks to, by the aid of’ (διὰ … Ἀθήνην) · also as adverb/preverb in tmesis with κοσμηθέντες (διὰ … κοσμηθέντες = διακοσμηθέντες ’drawn up in divisions’) · also + gen., ’through, among’ (διὰ μήλων ’among the flocks’) · also prep. + gen., ’through’ (διὰ πτόλιος ’through the city’) · also in tmesis with ἧκε (διὰ … ἧκε = διῆκε ’shot through’) · also in tmesis with ἦλθε (διὰ … ἦλθε = διῆλθε ’went through’)
διὶ: Ζεύς — Zeus, chief of the gods; masc. dat. sg.
δολίοιο: Δόλιος — Dolius, father of Melanthius; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
δολίος: Δόλιος — Dolius, father of Melantho; masc. nom. sg. · also the old Dolius who comes in from the fields with his sons and greets Odysseus (the household slave of Δολίον); masc. nom. sg.
δολίου: Δόλιος — Dolius, the old servant; masc. gen. sg.
δολιχόσκιον: δολιχόσκιος — long-shadowed; neut. acc. sg., epithet of a spear (ἔγχος)
δούπησεν: δουπέω — fall with a thud, thud; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable (= Attic ἐδούπησε): ’thudded down’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’ · also with opt., in a wish: ’if only’ (εἰ … ὁμοφρονέοις … γένοιο) · also ὡς εἰ + opt., ’as if’ (ὡς εἰ … ἱκοίατο ’as if they had come’) · also ὡς εἰ, ’as if’, before a noun with no verb of its own (ὡς εἰ κέρα … ἠὲ σίδηρος ’as if horn or iron’)
εἰδομένη: εἴδομαι — seem, make oneself like, appear as (+ dat.); pres. part. fem. nom. sg. · also functioning as aor. part. (the same -όμενος form serves both in Homer), ’having made herself like’ (Μέντορι εἰδομένη)
εἰδώς: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’knowing’
εἰπέ: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, tell; aor. imper. 2 sg.: ‘tell!’
εἰπὼν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.
εἴπω: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. subj. 1 sg.
εἴσατο: εἴδομαι — appear, seem, look like; aor. 3 sg. · also + dat. of a person: ’come into view, appear (to someone)’
εἴσεαι: οἶδα — know; fut. 2 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic εἴσῃ): ’you will know’
εἴσιδε: εἰσεῖδον (used as aor. of εἰσοράω) — catch sight of; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= εἰσεῖδε)
εἶδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg. (εἶδον ’I saw’) · also aor. 3 pl. (the form serves both persons): ’they saw’
εἷλεν: αἱρέω — take, seize, catch; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable (= εἷλε): ’caught’
εὐπείθης: Εὐπείθης — Eupeithes, father of Antinous; masc. nom. sg.
εὐρύοπα: εὐρύοπα — epithet of Zeus, literal sense disputed (’wide-voiced’ or ’far-seeing’); masc. nom. sg. in short -α
ζεύς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle · also with the relative ὅθι, no connective force: ὅθι θ’ ’where’ · also epic τε after a relative, no connective force (οὕς θ’ ’which’) · also epic τε after οὐδέ, no connective force: οὐδέ θ’ ἅλεσσι ’nor … with salt’
θαρσύνων: θαρσύνω — encourage, hearten; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’heartening’
θεοὶ: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’) · also of a goddess (θεός is common gender) · also nom. sg. subject, of a god already introduced by epithets but not yet named: ’the god’ · also nom. sg. in apposition to a name following: θεὸς … Ἑρμείας ’a god, Hermes’
θεῖος: θεῖος — divine, god-inspired; masc. nom. sg.
θυγάτηρ: θυγάτηρ — daughter; nom. sg. · also the nominative form used as a vocative: ’daughter!’ (the true vocative is θύγατερ)
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
θᾶσσον: ταχύς — swift; comparative adv. θᾶσσον ’more swiftly, the sooner’
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὃς δέ κ’ … ἵκηται ’whoever comes’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κ’ ἐλθὼν … εἴποιμι ’and I would go and tell’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καί νύ κ’ … ἔδυ ’and … would have set’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (τοὺς δέ κ’ … θέλξει ’and then … will enchant them’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ μέν κ’ αἰνήσωσι ’if they approve’) · also + opt. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (τόν κ’ εἴ μοι δοίης ’if you would give me him’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κ’ αὐτὸν γνώω ’if I come to know him’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κ’ … ἐρεθίζω ’so that I may provoke’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that’ (ὥς κ’ … ἵκηται ’so that he may reach’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if you should wish’ (αἴ κ’ ἐθέλῃσθα)
κέκλυτε: κλύω — hear, listen; aor. imper. 2 pl., reduplicated (κέκλυτε)
κίεν: κίω — go, go one’s way; impf. 3 sg., epic unaugmented (= ἔκιεν): ’went’
κακότητι: κακότης — badness, misery, distress; fem. dat. sg.
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ἦμαρ: ’evil’ (κακὸν ἦμαρ ’the evil day’) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’base, cowardly’ (κακὸν καὶ ἀνήνορα ’base and unmanned’) · also neut. acc. sg. attributive with πῆμα: ’evil’ (πῆμα κακὸν ’evil harm’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: κακὸν … βάζειν ’(it is) bad to speak’ · also neut. acc. sg. governed by ἐς: ’into evil’ (ἐς κακὸν … βάλῃσθα) · also neut. acc. sg. subject of an infinitive: ’an evil’ (κακὸν ἔμμεναι ’that an evil is’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of εἴη: ’evil’ (μή τι κακὸν … εἴη ’and may no evil be’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ῥάκος: ’vile’ (ῥάκος ἄλλο κακὸν ’another, a vile rag’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a finite verb: ’an evil’ (ἐπεὶ κακὸν ἔμπεσεν οἴκῳ ’since an evil fell upon the house’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with γενοίμην: ’a bane, an evil (to them)’ · also masc. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’a base man’ (κακὸς κακὸν ἡγηλάζει) · also masc. acc. sg., attributive with θάνατον: ’evil’ (θάνατον … κακόν ’evil death’) · also masc. acc. sg., in apposition to τινα: ’bad (man)’ (οὐ κακὸν οὐδὲ … ἐσθλόν ’neither bad nor good’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., attributive with τέλος: ’evil’ (κακὸν τέλος ’evil end’)
κακῇσι: κακός — bad, evil, grievous; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic κακαῖς)
καρήνων: κάρηνον — head, peak, summit; neut. gen. pl.
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’) · also + acc., of place, ’along’ (κατ’ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα ’along the misty paths’) · also + acc., ‘over against’ (κατ’ ἄντηστιν ‘right opposite’)
καταπαυέμεν: καταπαύω — stop, put an end to; pres. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic καταπαύειν)
κατόπισθε: κατόπισθε(ν) — behind, after; adv., or prep. + gen.: ’behind’

κείνους: κεῖνος (= ἐκεῖνος) — that, that one; demonstr. pron., masc. acc. pl.: ’those men’
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. κιόντες: κίω — go; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’going’
κούρη: κούρη — girl, daughter; fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg., in address: ’daughter’ (θάρσει, Ἰκαρίου κούρη ’take heart, daughter of Icarius’)
κούρῃ: κούρη — girl, maiden, daughter (Attic κόρη); dat. sg.
κρειόντων: κρείων — ruling, lord; masc. gen. pl., partitive: ’among those who rule’
κρονίδη: Κρονίδης — son of Cronus, patronymic/epithet of Zeus; voc. sg.

λαερτιάδη: Λαερτιάδης — son of Laertes, patronymic of Odysseus; voc. sg.
λαὸν: λαός — people, host; masc. acc. sg.
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl., governed by ἄνασσε ’was lord over’ · also gen. with a noun: ’of the people’ (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’) · also governed by ἐκ: ἔκ ... λαῶν ’from the people’ · also partitive gen. after a relative: οἵ ... λαῶν ἡμετέρων ’those of our people who’ · also partitive gen. after an adjective of rank: πάντων ἀριδείκετε λαῶν ’most distinguished of all the people’ · also gen. governed by πρόσθεν: ’before (the city and) the people’ · also gen. governed by φείδεο ’spare’: ’spare your people’ (φείδεο λαῶν σῶν)
λιλαιόμενοι: λιλαίομαι — long for, desire (+ gen.); pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl.: ’longing for’
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγαρον: μέγαρον — hall, main room of the house; acc. sg.
μέδων: Μέδων — Medon, herald of Odysseus’s household; masc. nom. sg.
μένος: μένος — force, might, spirit, drive; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject (μένος … ἐνέστακται ’his force has been instilled’) · also neut. nom. sg. in the periphrasis ἱερὸν μένος Ἀλκινόοιο: ’the sacred strength of Alcinous’, a periphrasis for Alcinous himself
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’ · also ’lest’ + subj. after a past verb of urging (κελόμην … μή … λάθηται ’I urged … lest he forget’) · also in a condition, ’if … not’ (εἰ … μή τίς σε βιάζεται) · also with an infinitive used as an imperative, a prohibition: μή μ’ … καταλείπειν ’do not leave me’ · also negating a purpose clause after ἵνα: ’so that … not’ (ἵνα μή τι … ἀλγήσετε ’so that you may not suffer’) · also with the optative, a negative wish: ’may … not’ (μή … ἀντιβολήσαις) · also ὡς ἂν μή + subj., negative purpose: ’so that … not’ (ὡς ἂν μή σε κατατρύχῃ ’so that he may not wear you out’) · also + subj. giving the content of an oath, ’that no one …’ (ὀμόσσατε … μή τις … πλήξῃ ’swear that no one strike’) · also μή + subj. standing alone as a warning, ’lest’ (μή τίς τοι … ἀναστῇ ’lest someone rise up against you’) · also μή + fut. indic. in a fear clause: ’lest, I fear’ (μή τίς … νεμεσήσεται ’lest anyone resent’)
μαστορίδης: Μαστορίδης — son of Mastor, patronymic of Halitherses; masc. nom. sg.
μεγάλοιο: μέγας — great; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
μεγάρων: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. gen. pl.
μεμαυῖαν: μάω (perf. μέμαα) — be eager, strive; perf. part. fem. acc. sg.: ’eager, clamouring’
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after, in quest of; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (μετ’ … βαῖνε = μετέβαινε ’followed’) · also + dat., ’among, between’ (μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισιν ’between the two of them’) · also + gen., ’among, in company with’ (μετ’ ἄλλων … ἑταίρων ’among your other companions’)
μετέειπε: μετεῖπον — speak among, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic μετεῖπε)
μεταλλᾷς: μεταλλάω — inquire after, ask about; pres. 2 sg.
μευ: ἐγώ — I; encl. gen. sg., epic μευ (= Attic μου): ’of me’, with κλύω ’hear me’ · also gen. with ἄγχι: ’near me’ (μευ ἄγχι στᾶσα) · also gen. of possession, ’my’ (οἵ μευ … κῆρ ’my heart’) · also gen. sg. with a participle: ’of me hearing’ (μευ ἀκούοντος, with φίλον ἦτορ ’heart’) · also gen. with κήδομαι: ’care for me’ (ἦ μευ … κήδεαι ’you care for me’)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’) · also dat. of possession with a noun: ’my’ (νηῦς δέ μοι ἥδ’ ἕστηκεν ’this ship of mine stands’)
μύθων: μῦθος — speech, word, thing said (not yet ’myth’ in Homer); gen. pl.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’ · also ’lest’ in a warning, + 2 sg. fut./subj.: μὴ … ἀποτίσεαι ’lest you pay for it’ · also + inf., negating an infinitive of advice that gives the content of a word: ’not to’ (ἔπος … μὴ πάντα μνηστῆρσιν ὁμιλεῖν ’a word, not to mingle in everything with the suitors’) · also negating a generic relative clause with the subj.: ᾧ μὴ πολλοὶ ἔωσιν ’who has not many’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
μῦθος: μῦθος — speech, word, thing said; masc. nom. sg.
νέεσθαι: νέομαι — go, return home; pres. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic νεῖσθαι)
νεφεληγερέτα: νεφεληγερέτα — epithet of Zeus: ’cloud-gatherer’ (νεφέλη ’cloud’ + ἀγείρω ’gather’); masc. nom. sg., old -α form
νεῖκος: νεῖκος — quarrel, strife; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’a quarrel (arises)’
νύ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’) · also encl. dat. sg. of the possessor with a body part: ’his’ (ἀνὰ ῥῖνας δέ οἱ ’up his nostrils’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἵδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’these here’
οἶκτος: οἶκτος — pity, compassion; masc. nom. sg.
οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg.
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὐκέτι: οὐκέτι — no longer, not any more; adv.
οὐλύμποιο: Ὄλυμπος — Olympus; gen. sg., epic Οὐ- lengthening and genitive in -οιο (= Attic Ὀλύμπου)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg.: ’all’ (πάντα δῆμον ’all the people’) · also neut. acc. pl. adverbial: ’altogether, in every respect’ (οὐκ ἄρα πάντα νοήμονες ’not altogether sensible’)
πάντας: πᾶς — all, every; masc. acc. pl.
πάρος: πάρος — before, formerly; adv., with inf. like Attic πρίν · also a plain temporal adverb with a finite verb, not paired with an infinitive: ’formerly, in the past’ (αἳ πάρος ἦσαν ’who formerly were’) · also ’before (that)’ with a finite verb, in the past: πάρος δ’ εἰς Ἴλιον ᾤχετο ’before that he went to Ilios’ · also with a participle: ’formerly, before’ (πάρος περ ἐὼν ’though formerly being’) · also bare adv. after ἠέ ’than’, with no verb: ’before, formerly’ (μείζονα … ἠὲ πάρος ’taller than before’)
πάτερ: πατήρ — father; voc. sg. · also πατέρα, masc. acc. sg., elided (πάτερ’ = πατέρα): ’father’ (μητρὸς … πάτερ’ ’mother’s father’)
πέρι: περί — around, about, exceedingly; adv. with anastrophe (accent thrown back): ’beyond all others’ (πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν) · also preposition with anastrophe + acc., of place: ’around’ (ἄστυ πέρι ’around the city’) · also preposition with anastrophe + gen.: ’about, concerning’ (φόνου πέρι ’about slaughter’)
παιδὸς: παῖς — child, daughter; fem. gen. sg. (φίλης ... παιδός ’a dear daughter’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’son’ (παιδὸς ἐμοῖο ’my son’; τοῦ παιδὸς ἀγαυοῦ ’the noble son’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’boy, child’, with ἐόντος, gen. of the person described (παιδὸς ἐόντος ’when I was a boy’)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παρισταμένη: παρίσταμαι — stand beside, come to one’s side; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.
πατρί: πατήρ — father; masc. dat. sg. · also masc. dat. sg. after ἐπιπείθομαι, ’obey’: ’(obeyed his) father’ (φίλῳ ἐπεπείθετο πατρί)
πεπνυμένα: πέπνυμαι — be prudent, wise (perf. w/ pres. sense, from πνέω ’breathe’); part. neut. acc. pl.: ’prudent (counsels)’
πεπνυμένος: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. nom. sg. (trad. linked to πνέω ’breathe’, though uncertain), stock epithet: ’prudent’
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’) · also adverb of place, no case: ’round about’ (περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ’and round it a fence is driven’) · also + dat., of the thing fought over: ’over, for’ (περὶ κτεάτεσσι μαχειόμενος ’fighting over possessions’) · also + gen., of the thing fought over: ’over, for’ (fighting over a person) · also + acc. of the occupation: ’about, at’ (περὶ δεῖπνον πένοντο ’busied themselves about the meal’)
πεσών: πίπτω — fall; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having fallen’
πιστὰ: πιστός — trustworthy, to be trusted; neut. nom. pl., ἐστί understood: οὐκέτι πιστά ’no longer is there trust’
ποιμένι: ποιμήν — shepherd; masc. dat. sg., in the standing royal title ποιμὴν λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’
πολέμοιο: πόλεμος — war, battle; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
πολυμήχαν: πολυμήχανος — many-devising; voc. sg., elided (πολυμήχαν’ = πολυμήχανε)
πολύτλας: πολύτλας — much-enduring; adj., masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Odysseus (πολύ ’much’ + root of τλῆναι ’endure’)
πολὺ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’by far’ · also neut. nom. sg. adj. agreeing with ὕδωρ: ’much, plentiful’ · also neut. acc. sg. adverbial with a negative: ’far’ (οὐ πολὺ ναῖεν ’did not live far off’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with κάλλος: ’much’ (κάλλος πολύ ’much beauty’)
πού: πού — somewhere; enclitic adv., weakened to ’I suppose, perhaps’
προΐει: προΐημι — send forth, send along; impf. 3 sg.: ’sent along’
προπάροιθ: προπάροιθε(ν) — in front of, before (+ gen.); prep., elided (προπάροιθ’)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
προσεφώνεεν: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεφώνει)
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
προτέρω: πρότερος — before, further; neut. comp. adv. προτέρω: ’further in’
πρόσθε: πρόσθε — before, in front; adv. · also prep. + gen.: ’in front of’ (πρόσθε ποδῶν ’before his feet’)
πρὸ: πρό — before, in front; prep. + gen.; also adv. or preverb in tmesis, ’ahead, forward’ (πρὸ … ἔαξεν ’broke ahead’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’ · also + gen., ’in the eyes of, with’ (πρὸς πόσιός τε καὶ υἱέος ’in the eyes of her husband and son’)
πτερόεντα: πτερόεις — winged (πτερόν ’feather, wing’); neut. acc. pl.: ’winged (words)’
πτολέμου: πτόλεμος — war, battle; masc. gen. sg., epic form (= Attic πολέμου)
πως: πώς — somehow, in any way; enclitic adv. (οὔ πως ’in no way’)
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.
πᾶσαν: πᾶς — all, every; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with ἰθύν: ’for every (undertaking)’ · also ’the whole’ (of a single extent, not distributive ’every’): πᾶσαν ἠοίην ’the whole morning’, acc. of duration · also agreeing with ὑπερβασίην: ’all, the whole of’ (πᾶσαν … ὑπερβασίην ’all their transgression’)
πῖπτε: πίπτω — fall; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔπιπτε)
σμερδαλέον: σμερδαλέος — terrible, dreadful; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’terribly’
στῆ: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔστη): ’stood’
σφ: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. pron., elided σφ’ for dat. σφι ’for them’ or acc. σφε ’them’
σφεας: σφεῖς — they; epic acc. pl. pron.: ’them’
σφιν: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. dat. pl./sg. pron.: ’to/for them’
σχεδὸν: σχεδόν — near, close by (+ gen.); adv. · also + dat.: σχεδὸν ἀλλήλῃσι ’close to one another’
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’ · also after ἤ ’than’, with no connective force: ἤ τ’ οἰωνοί ’than birds’ · also after ὅ ‘that’, with no connective force: ὅ τ’ οὐκέτι νόστιμός ἐστιν ‘that he is no longer returning’
τάδ: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. acc. pl., elided (τάδ’ = τάδε): ’these things’
τάδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also with a noun, neut. acc. pl.: ’these’ (τάδε δώμαθ’ ’this house’, plural for one dwelling)
τάφος: τάφος — amazement, astonishment; masc. nom. sg. · also τάφος — tomb, burial; masc. nom. sg. (homograph)
τάχιστα: ταχύς — quick, swift; superl. neut. acc. pl. as adv. τάχιστα: ’most quickly’
τέ: τε — and; enclitic connective, also marks a standing fact (epic τε) · also in the idiom ὅ τε (= ὅτι) ’in that, because’, giving a reason: ὅ τέ με … ἀποβῆναι ἀνώγει ’in that he bids me step off’ · also in ἦ τέ, a strengthened affirmation: ’truly’ (ἦ τέ μ’ ἔφαντο ’who truly said’)
τέκνον: τέκνον — child; neut. voc. sg. (= nom./acc. in form)
τέσσαρες: τέσσαρες — four; numeral, masc. nom. pl. (Attic τέτταρες)
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj. · also plain interrogative, direct object/predicate: ’what’ (τί πάθω ’what am I to suffer’; τί ... γένηται ’what is to become’) · also the enclitic indefinite as an adjective agreeing with a noun, accented before enclitic που: εἴ τί που εἴλυμα ’if any wrapper’ · also enclitic indefinite with a negative, ’anything’, as accusative subject of an infinitive (οὐ … τί φημι κακώτερον ἄλλο … συγχεῦαι ’I say nothing else is worse’) · also enclitic indefinite, adverbial without a negative: ’somehow, in some way’ (τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ’this seems to me somehow the fairest’) · also enclitic indefinite as an adjective after μή, accented before an enclitic: ’any’ (μή τί τοι … πῆμα ’any harm to you’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ὅπως, accented before enclitic μοι: ’any’ (τί … ἄλγος ’any pain’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ἤ, accented before the enclitic μοι: ’any’ (ἤ τί μοι … κειμήλιον ’or any treasure of mine’) · also the enclitic indefinite as a substantive object after εἴ: ’anything’ (εἴ τί μιν εἴποι ’whether she would say anything to him’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective, accented before enclitic μοι: ’some’ (σῆμά τί μοι ’some sign for me’)
τίθησθα: τίθημι — put, place, make; pres. 2 sg., epic -σθα (= Attic τίθης): ’you put, make’
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταμόντες: τάμνω (τέμνω) — cut; aor. part. masc. nom. pl., epic τάμνω (= Attic τεμόντες): ’having cut’
ταῦτα: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεύχε: τεῦχος — armour, gear (pl. τεύχεα); neut. acc. pl., elided (τεύχε’ = τεύχεα)
τεύχεα: τεῦχος — tool, gear, armor, equipment; neut. nom./acc. pl.
τεὸν: τεός (epic possessive = σός) — your, yours; masc./neut. acc. sg.
τηλέμαχ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. voc. sg., elided (Τηλέμαχ’ = Τηλέμαχε)
τηλέμαχον: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. acc. sg.
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’ · also as a substantive object in a statement: ’something’ (καί τι ἴσασι ’they know something’) · also neut. acc. sg. as object with a negative: ’anything’ (οὐδέ τι ῥέξαι ’nor to have done anything’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also with a negative: ’any, anyone’ (οὐ … τις ’no one’; οὐδέ τις ’nor any’) · also after the relative ὅς, indefinite: ὅς τις ’whichever, whoever’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl.: ’they’; also relative: ’who’ · also τοι, the affirming particle (ἀλλ’ ἦ τοι ’but truly’), as the grave-accented form τοὶ
τοὺς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. pl. ’them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. pl. τοῖς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: masc./neut. dat. pl. ’in which, with which’ (τετυγμένα, τοῖς ἐνάμελγεν ’well-made, in which he milked’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. dat. pl.: ’the’ (ἰχθύσι τοῖς ὀλίγοισι ’for the little fishes’) · also demonstrative dat. pl. of things just named, ‘with these’ (τοῖς ἔξειμι ‘with these I shall go out’)

ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’ · also introducing the first alternative of a deliberation: ’whether … or’ (ἢ ἐλάσει’ … ἦέ μιν ἦκ’ ἐλάσειε) · also ’than’ after a word of difference (ἀλλοῖον … ἢ Ὀδυσῆ’ ’another … than Odysseus’) · also the first of two alternatives: ’either … or’ (ἢ στοναχῆς ἠὲ κτύπου ’either groaning or noise’)
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤϊον: εἶμι — go; impf. 3 pl., epic ἤϊον (Attic ᾖσαν)
ἥδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., fem. nom. sg.
ἥρως: ἥρως — hero, man of standing; masc. nom. sg. · also used as a vocative in direct address, inserted mid-sentence (ἥρως, εἴρεσθαι δέ ’and ask, hero that you are’), distinct from its use as a narrative title ’the hero’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦλθεν: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’came’
ἦρχε: ἄρχω — begin, rule; impf. 3 sg., + gen. ’began (the speaking)’ · also ’go first, lead the way’ (no gen.): ἦρχε δ’ Ἀθήνη ’and Athena went first, led the way’ · also + gen. of the way: ἦρχε ὁδοῖο ’led the way’ · also absolute: ’ruled, was king’
ἰδὼν: ὁράω (aor. stem εἰδ-) — see; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ἰδών): ’seeing’
ἰθακήσιοι: Ἰθακήσιος — man of Ithaca; masc. voc. pl. · also masc. nom. pl., subject: ’the Ithacans’ (Ἰθακήσιοι εἰσορόωσι ’the Ithacans look upon’)
ἰών: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἴδοι: ὁράω (aor. stem ἰδ-) — see; aor. opt. 3 sg., purpose after ὡς: ’might see’
ἴομεν: εἶμι — go; pres. subj. 1 pl. (hortatory): ’let us go’ · also subj. in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’we go, are going’ (ὄφρ’ ἂν … ἀγροὺς ἴομεν ’while we go through the fields’)
ἴσχεο: ἴσχω — hold, restrain; pres. imper. mid. 2 sg., epic -εο (= Attic ἴσχου): ’restrain yourself, hold back’
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense · also relative ’where’ + indic.: ἵνα … καθεύδετον ’where the two are sleeping’ · also + opt. after a future main verb: ’so that … may’ (ἄξω … ἵνα … ἄλφοι ’I will take … so that he may bring in’)
ὀβριμοπάτρης: ὀβριμοπάτρη — she of the mighty father (ὄβριμος + πατήρ); fem. gen. sg., epithet of Athena
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. acc. sg., double-σ form (metrical variant of Ὀδυσῆα)
ὀδυσῆ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. acc. sg. Ὀδυσῆα, elided (Ὀδυσῆ’ = Ὀδυσῆα)
ὀδυσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆος)
ὀδυσῆϊ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. dat. sg., epic Ὀδυσῆϊ (single σ, diaeresis; = Ὀδυσσῆϊ, Attic Ὀδυσσεῖ)
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’) · also article-like with a superlative: ’the worst’ (ὁ κάκιστος Ἀχαιῶν ’the worst of the Achaeans’)
ὁμοιΐου: ὁμοίϊος (= ὅμοιος) — impartial, common to both sides (sense disputed); masc. gen. sg., with πολέμοιο
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὄλεσαν: ὄλλυμι — destroy; aor. 3 pl. act., unaugmented (Attic ὤλεσαν)
ὄπα: ὄψ (gen. ὀπός) — voice; fem. acc. sg., epic ὄπα
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅπως: ὅπως — so that, in order that, how; + subj. or fut. indic. · also + opt., in secondary sequence after a past-tense verb, indirect deliberative: ’how it might’ (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’) · also ’when’ = ὅτε · also ’as, however’ + subj. in a general clause: ὅπως ἐθέλῃσιν ’however he wishes’ · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a past tense: ’so that … might follow’ (ὅπως … ἑποίατο) · also + pres. indic., ’as, in whatever way’ (ὅπως ἐθέλεις ’as you wish’) · also ’how’ + aor. indic., indirect question after a verb of telling (κατάλεξον ὅπως ἤντησας ’tell how you came upon’)
ὅρκια: ὅρκιον — oath, sworn pledge; neut. acc. pl.: ὅρκια δοῦναι ’give oaths, swear’
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅττι: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; epic neut. nom./acc. sg. ὅττι (= Attic ὅ τι) · also with a superlative, ’as … as possible’ (ὅττι τάχιστα ’as quickly as possible’) · also in an indirect question, ’what’ (ὅττι ἑ κήδοι ’what was troubling him’) · also conj. ’that, because’, introducing a clause (ὅττι μιν ὣς ὑπέδεκτο ’that he had received him so’)
ὑμετέρῃ: ὑμέτερος — your (pl.); adj., fem. dat. sg.
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’) · also adverbial, of breeding: ’begotten under, born of’ (ὑπὸ δ’ ἡμίονοι ’and under them [the mares], mules’) · also + dat., marking the agent with a passive verb: ’by’ (ὑπὸ μνηστῆρσιν δαμείη ’be overcome by the suitors’) · also + gen., ’from under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο) · also + gen., marking agent with a passive verb/participle beyond dying, ’by’: μεγάλου ὑπὸ κύματος ἀρθείς ’lifted up by a great wave’ · also + gen., of cause: ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς ’at the rush (of the throw)’
ὕπατε: ὕπατος — highest, supreme; masc. voc. sg.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’) · also ὡς ὅθ’ (= ὡς ὅτε), ’as when’, comparing with an occasion in the past (ὡς ὅθ’ ὑπὸ Τροίην ’as when beneath Troy’) · also introducing an indirect statement after a verb of saying: ’that, how’ (εἴποιμ’ ὡς … ἔρχομαι ’I might tell how I am coming’) · also ὡς ἄν + opt., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἄν τίς σε … μακαρίζοι ’so that someone … would call you blessed’) · also ὡς + participle, ’as one who’ (ὡς ἐκ θανάτοιο φυγόντα ’as one escaped from death’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν … ἔρχησθον ’so that you two may go’) · also ὡς = ’to, toward’ + acc. of a person (ὡς τὸν ὁμοῖον ’to the like’) · also exclamatory ὡς + finite verb: ’how’ (ὡς ὁ μολοβρὸς … ἀγορεύει ’how the glutton talks’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’ · also introducing a wish with the optative: ’so may…’ (ὣς ἔμ’ ἀϊστώσειαν ’so may they make me vanish’)
ὤρνυντο: ὄρνυμι — stir, rouse; mid. bestir oneself, rise; impf. 3 pl., + inf.: ’rose (to sleep)’
ὤτρυνε: ὀτρύνω — urge on, rouse; aor. 3 sg., with the temporal augment ο → ω
ὥς: ὥς — thus, so; also (with κε/ἄν + subj.) ’so that, in order that’; adverb/conjunction · also introducing an indirect question: ’how’ (ὥς κε νέηται ’how he is to return’, after φράσσεται) · or ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τε · also causal, ’since, seeing that’ (ὥς οἱ ἐναργὲς ὄνειρον ἐπέσσυτο ’since a vivid dream had come upon her’) · also with κεν + opt., purpose: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also ὥς ’just as’, in ὥς περ (accented before enclitic περ) (ὥς περ ὑπέστης ’just as you promised’) · also ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic με (ὥς με κελεύεις ’as you bid me’) · also postpositive after its noun, comparative ’like’ (οἰωνῶν ὥς ’like birds’) · also ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τοι (ὥς τοι ἐγὼν ἐρέω ’as I shall tell you’) · also correlative ’so’ answering ὅπως, introducing a wish with the opt., accented before the enclitic τοι: ’so may’ (ὥς τοι Ζεὺς τελέσειεν ’so may Zeus fulfil it for you’) · also with a plain subj. (no κε/ἄν), purpose: ’so that’ (ὥς τοι δῶρ’ ἀποπέμψω ’so that I may send you the gifts’) · also ὥς accented before enclitic οἱ, of measure: ’as much as’ (ὥς οἱ χεῖρες ἐχάνδανον ’as much as his hands could hold’) · also exclamatory, ’how’, accented before the enclitic τις (ὥς τις θαρσαλέος … ἐσσι ’how bold you are’) · also with the plain optative (no κε/ἄν), purpose, accented before the enclitic μιν: ’so that’ (ὥς μιν ψυχὴ λίποι ’so that life should leave him’) · also ὡς ’as, how’, accented before enclitic μοι (ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ’as it seems to me’) · also ὡς ’how’, introducing a narrated event, accented before the enclitic μιν (ὥς μιν θηρεύοντ’ ἔλασεν ’how he struck him as he hunted’) · also ὡς ’as, like’, accented before enclitic τις (ὥς τις ’like some’)
ὧδε: ὧδε — here, to this place, in this way; adv.
ᾕρει: αἱρέω — take, seize; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’seized’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
